claims.claim: Kotter frames management and leadership as two distinct, complementary systems: management copes with complexity through planning and budgeting, organizing and staffing, and controlling and problem-solving, while leadership copes with change through setting direction, aligning people, and motivating and inspiring them; both are needed.

James MacGregor Burns introduced the contrast between transforming and transactional leadership in 1978, and Bernard Bass extended the work in 1985, renaming the transforming style transformational and specifying four components: idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration.

Transactional leadership operates through exchange, in which a leader exchanges a reward or reinforcement for task accomplishment or applies correction for failure (contingent reward and management-by-exception), whereas transformational leaders raise followers to higher levels of motivation and morality; Bass held that a leader can display both.

Robert K. Greenleaf coined the term servant leadership in his 1970 essay 'The Servant as Leader,' defining the servant-leader as servant first: the natural desire to serve comes before the aspiration to lead.

Situational leadership, developed by Paul Hersey and Ken Blanchard beginning in 1969, holds that there is no single best leadership style; the leader should match a mix of directive (task) and supportive (relationship) behavior to the follower's readiness or development level for a specific task, ranging from directing to delegating.

The Healthcare Leadership Alliance, a consortium of six professional membership associations that includes the American College of Healthcare Executives, identified five common competency domains for practicing healthcare managers: communication and relationship management, leadership, professionalism, knowledge of the healthcare environment, and business skills and knowledge; the associated directory contains about 300 competency statements.

The American Hospital Association states that the role of a hospital or health-system governing board is to govern, not manage: the board selects, supports, advises, and evaluates the CEO; approves the mission, vision, and strategic direction and the strategic plan; approves financial and quality goals; and monitors performance, while the CEO runs day-to-day operations and executes strategy.

Medical and health services managers plan, direct, and coordinate healthcare organizations and were about 616,200 jobs in 2024 with a median annual wage of $117,960 (May 2024); the occupation typically requires at least a bachelor's degree.

No single leadership framework is established as best in all situations; situational leadership explicitly denies a single best style, and evidence linking transformational leadership to positive outcomes such as nurse engagement and retention is associational rather than a universal verdict.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether transactional and transformational leadership are opposite ends of one scale or independent behaviors a single leader can use together.
positions: Burns (1978) framed transforming and transactional leadership as broadly contrasting orientations.
Bass (1985) argued a single leader can display transactional and transformational behaviors simultaneously.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Presented Burns's contrast and Bass's extension in sequence, noting explicitly that Bass departed from Burns by allowing both styles at once, so the lesson does not force a false either/or.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Exact domain labels vary slightly across publications of the Healthcare Leadership Alliance and ACHE competency work.
positions: The Stefl (2008) HLA model names communication and relationship management, leadership, professionalism, knowledge of the healthcare environment, and business skills and knowledge.

A derived open-access competency article lists closely related labels (leadership; communication and relationship management; professional and social responsibility; health and healthcare environment; business).
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Used the canonical HLA five-domain naming from Stefl (2008) as authoritative and treated the derived article as corroboration of the same five-domain structure rather than a competing list.

sourceRecords.title: What Leaders Really Do
sourceRecords.notes: Best-of-HBR reprint of Kotter's classic article (originally 1990). Supports the framing that management copes with complexity (planning/budgeting, organizing/staffing, controlling) and leadership copes with change (direction, alignment, motivation), and that the two are complementary and both necessary. Read via HBR listing and corroborating search summaries; copyrighted, so described in original wording with no prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Measuring Transformational Leadership in Establishing Nursing Care Excellence
sourceRecords.notes: Open-access CC BY article. Confirms transformational leadership was originally conceptualized in the 1970s by Burns (1978) and expanded by Bass (1985); describes transactional leadership as exchange of reward/reinforcement for task accomplishment; lists the four components (idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, individualized consideration). Used to anchor attribution and the four I's; no prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: What Is Servant Leadership?
sourceRecords.provider: Robert K. Greenleaf Center for Servant Leadership
sourceRecords.notes: Publisher of Greenleaf's work. Confirms Greenleaf coined servant leadership in the 1970 essay 'The Servant as Leader' and the 'servant first' definition. Used for attribution and definition; the short 'servant first' phrase is Greenleaf's own and is attributed, not presented as EliExplains wording.

sourceRecords.title: Situational Leadership Theory (Hersey and Blanchard)
sourceRecords.provider: EBSCO Research Starters — Social Sciences and Humanities
sourceRecords.notes: Secondary reference. Confirms Hersey and Blanchard developed situational leadership (introduced in their 1969 'Management of Organizational Behavior'), that it holds there is no single best style, and that the leader flexes directive (task) and supportive (relationship) behavior to follower readiness/development level from directing to delegating. Used for attribution and the core mechanism; no prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Common Competencies for All Healthcare Managers: The Healthcare Leadership Alliance Model
sourceRecords.provider: Journal of Healthcare Management (Stefl ME, Bontempo CA), 53(6):360-373
sourceRecords.notes: Foundational peer-reviewed article on the HLA model. Establishes the five common competency domains (communication and relationship management, leadership, professionalism, knowledge of the healthcare environment, business skills and knowledge), the six-organization consortium including ACHE, and the ~300 competency statements in the directory. Abstract/citation read on the LWW journal site; competency text is copyrighted and described, not reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Development and Use of the Leadership Competencies for Healthcare Services Managers Assessment
sourceRecords.provider: Frontiers in Public Health, via PubMed Central PMC6403121
sourceRecords.notes: Open-access CC BY article. Corroborates that HLA/ACHE competencies were developed from job-analysis surveys and cluster around five interconnected domains, and that leadership is one domain among the five rather than standing apart. Used to corroborate the competency-model structure; no competency statement text reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Position Description for a Health System or Hospital Board Member
sourceRecords.notes: AHA Trustee Services guidance. States the board's role is to govern, not manage; lists board responsibilities (select/support/advise/evaluate the CEO; approve mission, vision, strategic direction and plan; approve financial and quality goals and monitor performance) and that board members respect responsibilities delegated to the CEO and management. Used for the board-CEO division of labor; described in original wording.
